description: Known-answer vectors for the clerk's count. `count` vectors give an input and either the exact output or the error code; `verify` vectors give an input, a recorded verdict and whether the verdict matches the count. Outputs compare as JSON values: member order doesn't matter, array order does. README.md defines the input, the output and every rule.

count.name: majority: abstentions count for quorum, not for the majority
majority: absent seats are neither present nor counted
supermajority 2/3: abstention left out of the fraction
supermajority with large terms is exact
unanimity: approvals and an abstention approve
veto: an unchallenged blocking finding with evidence rejects
veto: a blocking finding that stood its challenge rejects
veto: a refuted finding doesn't block
veto: a blocking finding without evidence doesn't block
veto: a non-blocking finding with evidence doesn't block
veto: blockers listed in the findings' order
veto: a blocker rejects even when every seat abstains
veto: below quorum is no quorum, blockers still listed
borda: picks b where the Condorcet winner is a
schulze: picks the Condorcet winner a
schulze: a Condorcet cycle is a tie
schulze: tie-break none is the default
schulze: the seeded tie-break picks the lowest hash (c)
borda: equal scores are a tie
borda: the seeded tie-break picks a over b
borda: a single winner never uses the tie-break
borda: abstentions count for quorum only
median: even count takes the lower middle
seeded tie-break on a yes/no rule
ballot from a seat not drawn
a ranking on a yes/no rule
a value on a yes/no rule
bad rule wins over bad quorum
bad seats wins over bad quorum

verify.name: a verdict that matches its ballots
an outcome the ballots don't give
a tally that doesn't match the ballots
a verdict with an extra member
a ranked verdict that names the Borda winner under Schulze
a tie broken without a seed
